chains.title: CEBPA site creation at the dELS increases SORT1 and is protective

links.claim: CEBPA binds this element. I choose CEBPA because E19 shows an exact CEBPA ChIP-seq peak containing this base in HepG2, and E04 lists CEBPA among bound, expressed TFs with a binding model in HepG2. The alt T allele is nominated to bind CEBPA more strongly than ref G because this is a C/EBP-site-creating 1p13 SORT1 mechanism, but no CEBPA QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific assay is supplied here, so the direction is the weakest link.
The variant lies in active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal; E03 scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not HepG2-specific.

The alt T allele is associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), and SORT1 has the strongest L2G score at this locus (0.99). This supports variant-to-SORT1 expression association, not element-to-SORT1 causality.

The relevant context is liver/hepatocyte-lineage: CEBPA has an exact ChIP-seq peak over this base in HepG2, and the SORT1 eQTL is observed in liver. HepG2 is a hepatoma stand-in for Hep 3B2.1-7, so this is indirect.

The G allele is the risk allele for high cholesterol/LDL in the strongest E15 associations, and the T allele is associated with higher SORT1 expression in E17. If higher hepatic SORT1 is protective, this is directionally consistent. However, one LDL trait reports T as effect allele and E18b says PSRC1-CELSR2-SORT1 protection may act via remnant cholesterol/CHD independent of LDL-C, so LDL-specific protection is not established.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA ChIP or EMSA will show stronger CEBPA binding to alt T than ref G at this base.
CRISPR editing of this base from G to T in a liver-cell context will increase SORT1 expression.
CEBPA knockdown will reduce the alt-T enhancer effect on SORT1.
falsified_if: No allele-specific CEBPA binding is detected at this base.
Editing this base alone does not change SORT1 enhancer activity or SORT1 expression in liver cells.
CEBPA knockdown does not affect the alt-T effect.

Editing this base alone will not change SORT1, CELSR2 or PSRC1 expression.

CRISPR editing of this base alone changes enhancer activity and SORT1, CELSR2 or PSRC1 expression in liver cells.
The eQTL and GWAS signals are shown to require this exact base rather than a linked variant.

chains.title: CEBPA site creation at the dELS increases CELSR2

links.claim: CEBPA binds this element. CEBPA is chosen because E19 shows an exact CEBPA ChIP-seq peak over this base in HepG2 and E04 lists CEBPA among bound, expressed TFs there. The alt T allele is nominated to bind CEBPA more strongly than ref G, but no CEBPA QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific assay is supplied, so the direction is unsupported.
The variant lies in active dELS EH38E1374646 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal; the E03 z-scores are biosample maxima, so HepG2-specific activity is not directly shown.

The alt T allele is associated with higher CELSR2 expression in liver (NES +1.04, p 9.4e-34), and CELSR2 has high L2G scores (0.96-0.98). E01 also annotates the variant as a CELSR2 3_prime_UTR_variant, so a direct transcript/3'UTR effect remains an alternative.
Liver/hepatocyte-lineage is relevant: CEBPA has an exact ChIP-seq peak in HepG2 and CELSR2 has a liver eQTL. The HepG2-to-Hep3B2.1-7 substitution is indirect.

G is the risk allele for high cholesterol/LDL in the strongest E15 traits, and T increases CELSR2 in E17; this is directionally consistent if higher CELSR2 is protective. But one LDL trait reports T as effect allele and E18b describes CHD protection via remnant cholesterol independent of LDL-C, so the LDL-specific claim is not established.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA binding at this base will correlate more strongly with CELSR2 than with SORT1 expression.
The CELSR2 liver eQTL will require this dELS and CEBPA.
A CELSR2 3'UTR reporter will not explain the full allelic effect if the enhancer mechanism is correct.
falsified_if: No allele-specific CEBPA binding is detected at this base.
CELSR2 expression is not affected by this dELS in liver cells.
The CELSR2 signal is fully explained by a direct 3'UTR effect rather than enhancer activity.

chains.title: FOXA1 site creation at the dELS increases SORT1

links.claim: FOXA1 binds this element. I choose FOXA1 because E05 reports 9 FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks containing this base in HepG2 and high expression in Hep3B2.1-7 (53.15 TPM, rank 84 of 1626 TFs), and E04 lists FOXA1 among bound, expressed TFs with a binding model in HepG2. The alt T allele is nominated to bind FOXA1 more strongly than ref G, but no FOXA1 QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific assay is supplied, so this direction is weak.
The variant lies in active dELS EH38E1374646 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal; E03 scores are maxima over biosamples, not HepG2-specific.

The alt T allele is associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), and SORT1 has the strongest L2G score (0.99). This supports variant-to-SORT1 association, not FOXA1 mediation.

The relevant context is liver/hepatocyte-lineage: FOXA1 has exact ChIP-seq peaks over this base in HepG2 and high expression in Hep3B2.1-7, and SORT1 has a liver eQTL. HepG2 is a stand-in for Hep3B2.1-7.

G is the risk allele for high cholesterol/LDL in the strongest E15 traits, and T increases SORT1 in E17; this is directionally consistent if higher SORT1 is protective. But one LDL trait reports T as effect allele and E18b says protection may be via remnant cholesterol/CHD independent of LDL-C, so LDL-specific protection is not established.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP will show stronger FOXA1 binding to alt T than ref G at this base.
FOXA1 knockdown, not CEBPA knockdown, will blunt the alt-T enhancer effect on SORT1.
CRISPR editing this base will change FOXA1 occupancy and SORT1 expression in liver cells.
falsified_if: No allele-specific FOXA1 binding is detected at this base.
FOXA1 knockdown does not affect enhancer activity or SORT1 expression.
CEBPA, not FOXA1, explains the allele-specific effect.

E17 provides a liver SORT1 eQTL, and E04 reports CEBPA ChIP occupancy in HepG2, used as the stand-in liver cancer line. Caveat: HepG2 is not Hep 3B2.1-7 or primary hepatocyte.

However, one LDL cholesterol trait reports effect allele T, and E18b says hepatic PSRC1-CELSR2-SORT1 protects against CHD via remnant cholesterol reduction independent of LDL-C; the LDL-protection claim is overclaimed and partly conflicting.
Same CEBPA issue as H1: E04 gives generic CEBPA occupancy in HepG2 but no allele-specific binding or CEBPA QBiC-SELEX direction. The alt-T stronger binding claim is unsupported.

E17 provides a PSRC1 liver eQTL and E04 reports CEBPA occupancy in HepG2. The HepG2/Hep 3B2.1-7 equivalence is still indirect.

The same phenotype-direction conflict applies: most E15 high-cholesterol/LDL associations point to G risk and E17 T increases PSRC1, but one LDL trait reports T as effect allele, and E18b says the protective CHD effect is via remnant cholesterol independent of LDL-C. PSRC1's L2G is also weaker.

grades_final.reason: E19 provides a CEBPA ChIP-seq peak containing this base in HepG2, and E04 lists CEBPA as bound/expressed there, so occupancy is supported. However, there is no CEBPA QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific assay showing alt T binds more strongly than ref G; the claimed direction is a prediction, so the binding link is only weak.

E03 directly annotates the variant within cCRE EH38E1374646, a dELS, with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal. The caveat that these z-scores are biosample maxima affects cell-type specificity, not the element annotation itself.

E17 shows the alt T allele associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), and E16 gives SORT1 the strongest L2G score (0.99). This supports variant-to-SORT1 expression association, though not element-to-SORT1 causality.

CEBPA occupancy is shown in HepG2, a hepatoma proxy, and SORT1 has a liver eQTL, but there is no direct CEBPA occupancy or expression evidence in the specified Hep3B2.1-7 context. The cell-type link is therefore indirect.

E15 supports strong LDL/cholesterol association with G as the risk allele in the strongest traits, and E17 shows T increases SORT1, which is directionally consistent if higher SORT1 is protective. But E15 also contains an LDL trait with T as effect allele, and E18b supports CHD protection via remnant cholesterol independent of LDL-C, so LDL-specific protection is not established.

E19 and E04 support CEBPA occupancy over this base in HepG2, but no CEBPA QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding assay shows that alt T binds CEBPA more strongly than ref G. Occupancy alone makes the binding/direction link weak.

E03 directly places the variant in active dELS EH38E1374646 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 marks. The biosample-maximum caveat limits cell-type-specific inference but does not undermine the element annotation.

E17 shows alt T associated with higher CELSR2 expression in liver (NES +1.04, p 9.4e-34), and E16 gives high CELSR2 L2G scores (0.96-0.98). This supports variant-to-CELSR2 expression association, with E01 raising a direct 3'UTR alternative rather than invalidating the association.
CEBPA ChIP is in HepG2 rather than the specified Hep3B2.1-7 cell line, though the liver eQTL supports a hepatocyte-lineage context. The cell-type evidence is relevant but indirect.

The strongest E15 cholesterol/LDL traits have G as risk allele, and E17 shows T increases CELSR2, which could be protective if higher CELSR2 is beneficial. But the effect-allele direction is mixed across LDL traits, and E18b describes protection via remnant cholesterol/CHD independent of LDL-C, so a CELSR2-specific LDL effect is not established.

E05 provides FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks containing this base in HepG2 and high FOXA1 expression in Hep3B2.1-7, supporting occupancy. However, there is no FOXA1 QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific assay showing alt T binds more strongly than ref G, so the direction claim remains weak.

E03 directly annotates the variant within active dELS EH38E1374646 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal. The z-scores being biosample maxima limits cell-type specificity but does not change the supported element identity.
E17 shows alt T associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), and E16 gives SORT1 L2G 0.99. This supports variant-to-SORT1 expression association, not FOXA1 mediation.

E15 supports strong cholesterol/LDL association with G as risk allele, and E17 shows T increases SORT1, directionally consistent if higher SORT1 is protective. But one LDL trait reports T as effect allele, and E18b supports CHD protection via remnant cholesterol independent of LDL-C, so LDL-specific protection through FOXA1/SORT1 is not established.
